mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes at 90% confidence, or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the trigger is not followed by a decline in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the joint trigger does not produce a statistically significant negative return at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals improved residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the trigger is not followed by a positive return in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above their respective 6-month averages indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, resulting in neutral-to-negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the joint trigger does not precede a negative return in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) for five consecutive months signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces consumer spending and depresses corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met, or the trigger is not followed by a negative return in more than 40% of instances.
